title: Audit and remediate missing per-tenant tail signals causing opaque capacity regressions
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Summary: During a capacity regression on 2025-02-16 we observed elevated latency and increased 504s for several tenants. Initial incident handling restored traffic, but post-incident analysis revealed multiple observability blind spots that delayed diagnosis: missing per-tenant tail latency percentiles, dashboards that aggregated percentiles incorrectly as averages or sums, and tracing gaps across the KV cache -> Redis backpressure path. These gaps masked the real signal: a small subset of tenants experienced sustained KV-cache thrashing and Redis write backpressure leading to queue pressure and token generation stalls.

Why this ticket: This ticket consolidates the postmortem action items for repairing the signal chain, remediating dashboards, adding a lightweight runbook for tenant-tail capacity anomalies, and ensuring these signals are visible in Console within the next release. The goal is to reduce time-to-detect for tenant-level tail events from hours to under 10 minutes and to provide automated alerts tied to the runbook.

What went wrong (observability failures):
- No tenant-labeled P99/P999 ingress queue metrics across the front-door and per-route aggregates; only global percentiles existed.
- Grafana dashboards used rollup queries that unintentionally summed counters and then computed percentiles client-side, misrepresenting tail behavior.
- Traces lacked a stable correlation key for KV eviction events; sampled traces frequently omitted eviction spans.
- Redis backpressure path lacked end-to-end tracing: client -> cache -> redis calls were not correlated, so root cause hunting required expensive log joins.
- No automated alert for tenant-specific tail amplification (we only alerted on global error rate or overall latency).

Immediate mitigation already done:
- Turned on temporary tenant-labeling for ingress counters in the canary region to unblock debugging (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/812).
- Rolled a hotfix to correct a Grafana query that was summing counters before aggregation; dashboards in canary now show per-tenant percentiles correctly (Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant-tail).
- Added a short-term synthetic runner that exercises worst-case prompt lengths for suspect tenants to surface failures.

Longer-term remediation (this ticket):
- Add per-tenant P50/P95/P99/P999 time-series for ingress queue depth and per-route request latency with tenant metadata attached.
- Replace any rollup queries that compute percentile-like metrics via sum/mean transformations with server-side percentile histograms (Hornet/Prometheus histogram or native percentile store) to preserve tail fidelity.
- Instrument KV eviction and Redis write calls with a stable correlation_id propagated from the request id; ensure spans are always emitted even on fast-path evictions.
- Implement a console dashboard that highlights tenant tail anomalies (P99 relative delta vs baseline) and exposes the top-20 tenants by P99 increase.
- Build an automated alerting rule that triggers when a tenant P99 exceeds baseline by X% for Y minutes and automatically attaches the recommended runbook steps.
- Run an audit across existing dashboards to find misaggregations and fix them; add test coverage for dashboard queries in CI.

Acceptance criteria:
- Per-tenant P99/P999 metrics are present in production for all routes with retention >= 14d.
- New dashboard surfaces the top tenants and matches offline analysis for the Feb 16 incident.
- Tracing shows correlation_id across request -> KV -> Redis paths in >= 85% of sampled traces.
- Alert fires in staging for a synthetic tenant amplification test within 10 minutes.
- PR for telemetry changes reviewed and merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/834.

Artifacts and links:
- Incident timeline & postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2025-02-16+Capacity+Regression+Postmortem
- Hotfix PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/812, https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1295
- Dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant-tail
- Slack investigation thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C03INCIDENTS/p1676572800000000

Risks and trade-offs:
- Adding tenant labels to high-cardinality metrics will increase cardinality and metric storage costs; mitigation: only enable tenant-level percentiles for routes above a request-volume threshold and use aggregated tenant cohorts for low-volume tenants.
- Increasing trace sampling or forcing eviction spans may raise overhead; mitigation: sample more aggressively only for the first 10 minutes after alert and maintain low baseline sampling.

Owners:
- Telemetry work (histograms, tenant labeling): Priya Shah, SL: Instrumentation team.
- Dashboard and alerting: Liam O'Connor (assignee).
- Tracing correlation: Marco Ruiz.

This ticket is intended to coordinate the above deliverables and spawn smaller implementation tasks once the design is agreed in the next 48 hours.

steps_to_reproduce: Run synthetic runner that sends bursty long-context prompts for a single tenant until KV eviction occurs; observe P99 and queue depth metrics.
In a staging region, temporarily enable tenant-level labeling and reproduce the load pattern from the incident (payloads and timing in the postmortem confluence).
Check traces for correlation_id linking request->kv->redis and confirm eviction spans are present in at least 8/10 sampled traces.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant tail metrics (P99/P999) available in production for major routes with retention 14d.
Dashboard in Console surfaces top-20 tenants by P99 regression and matches offline incident repro.
Tracing correlation_id is present for request->cache->redis path in >=85% of post-alert samples.
Alerting rule triggers in staging for synthetic tenant amplification within 10 minutes and attaches runbook link.
